name: Exceptions Result patterns at boundaries
short_definition: Python services use exceptions for exceptional control flow internally, map domain errors to stable HTTP/problem details at the edge (FastAPI exception handlers), convert ValidationError to 422, never leak stack traces or secrets to clients, and optionally use Result/Either-style returns only at library boundaries where exceptions are too coarse — not as a blanket replacement for exceptions.
scope_in: Exception hierarchy design; domain vs infrastructure errors; FastAPI HTTPException RequestValidationError exception_handler; Problem+JSON / stable error codes; ValidationError mapping; logging + correlation ids; Result/Ok/Err patterns (returns) at pure boundaries; retry classification (transient vs permanent); partial failure in task groups (ExceptionGroup); SSE/error event shapes.
scope_out: Frontend toast UX; full OTel metrics catalog (see observability); auth scheme design details (py-auth-security); Temporal saga compensation (workers); Rust Result as language default (different culture).
defaults: Raise typed domain exceptions (AppError subclasses with code, http_status, safe_message, extra). Catch at framework boundary only — not every layer. FastAPI: register handlers for AppError, RequestValidationError, Exception (last-resort 500). Clients get {error: {code, message, details?, request_id}} — no stack. Log full exception with exc_info and request_id server-side. ValidationError/RequestValidationError → 422 with redacted details. Use HTTPException for simple one-off route errors; prefer domain errors for reusable logic. Retries only on transient infra errors (network, 503, deadlock) with budget. ExceptionGroup from TaskGroup: log all sub-exceptions. Result types optional inside pure parsing helpers; do not force Result through all async I/O code.
decision_gates: USE exceptions when: Python service business logic, FastAPI handlers, fail-fast setup (settings). USE Result/Ok-Err when: pure parse functions composing many fallible steps without try noise, or public library APIs where throwing is undesirable. USE HTTPException when: local to one route and no domain reuse. DO NOT use Result as enterprise-wide law in Python (fights idioms and FastAPI). DO NOT catch Exception broadly in domain services. Map DB integrity errors to 409/400 at repository boundary, not raw SQL to clients.
do_dont: DO: typed error codes (snake_case stable strings); include request_id; log once at boundary; reraise cancellation; preserve cause with raise X from e; map ValidationError.errors() carefully. DON'T: raise bare Exception/strings; return None for errors without types; expose e.args or SQL to clients; except: pass; log and re-raise as new without chain; use 500 for validation; mutate global error state; put secrets in error details; catch CancelledError as normal error.
failure_modes: 1) Stack traces in production JSON. 2) Double-logging (every layer logs). 3) 500 for bad input. 4) Lost cancellation. 5) ExceptionGroup only first error logged. 6) Retry storms on non-idempotent 500s. 7) Inconsistent error shapes across routes. 8) Validation details leak passwords. 9) Bare HTTPException(detail=str(e)) with internal info. 10) Domain layer depends on FastAPI HTTPException (untestable pure logic).
anti_patterns: except Exception as e: return {'error': str(e)}; raise Exception('fail'); error codes as free-form English only; Result monad through FastAPI dependency stack; silent pass; asserting isinstance of third-party exceptions without mapping; using assert for runtime validation in production paths; different error JSON per router; logging PII in error payloads.
tools: FastAPI/Starlette exception handlers; pydantic ValidationError; structlog/stdlib logging; optional returns / result packages only if team standardizes (default: small local Ok/Err or exceptions). Testing: pytest.raises, httpx ASGI test client for status codes. Schemathesis for error response schemas. Alternatives: HTTPX problem details libs — optional.
versions_as_of: as_of 2026-07-13: FastAPI 0.115+ / current 0.12x lines with exception_handler; Starlette HTTPException; Python 3.11+ ExceptionGroup native; pydantic v2 ValidationError.errors(). Prefer stdlib ExceptionGroup handling over third-party unless needed.

deprecation_watch: Flask-style broad try/except in each view without central handlers; returning tuples (data, error) inconsistently mixed with exceptions; Tornado-era patterns; exposing Werkzeug debugger in prod; GraphQL error extensions without redaction; using HTTP 200 for all errors with body flag (unless graph constraint — not REST default).
ts_boundary: Align error JSON with Next BFF expectations: stable code + message + request_id. TS Zod errors on BFF are separate from Python 422 — map both to user-safe UI messages. Propagate x-request-id both ways. Do not parse Python stack traces in TS. OpenAPI error schema should be shared/generated.
rust_boundary: Rust services prefer Result + thiserror/anyhow internally, map to HTTP at edge similarly. Cross-language: same error code vocabulary in OpenAPI. Do not throw Python exceptions across FFI without translation. For dual stacks, document shared error codes in contract repo.
supabase_boundary: PostgREST errors (JWT, RLS, unique violation) must be mapped — never raw to client. Distinct codes: rls_denied, conflict, not_found. service_role mistakes should 500+alert, not client detail. Prefer repository layer translating DBAPIError.
boundary_contracts: OpenAPI components for ErrorResponse; status code matrix (400 validation domain, 401/403 auth, 404, 409 conflict, 422 validation, 429, 500/503). MCP tools return isError with safe message. Webhooks: verify then return 2xx only after durable accept — use 4xx for bad signatures. Migrations errors are ops, not API.
decision_matrix_row: Problem: domain failure in Python API → typed AppError + handler. Problem: form validation in browser → TS Zod. Problem: systems-level recoverable errors in Rust → Result. Problem: multi-step compensation → Temporal/workflows, not ad-hoc exceptions.
threats: Information disclosure via error bodies; log injection via user-controlled messages; recon via distinct error codes on auth endpoints (user enumeration); DoS via expensive error formatting; stored XSS if error HTML-rendered (prefer JSON APIs).
mitigations: Uniform auth failure messages where enumeration matters; redact validation input_value; structured logging not string concat of raw headers; generic 500 message; rate limit; security review of error codes list; no HTML error pages for JSON APIs.
agent_codegen_policy: MUST: central exception handlers; typed AppError; 422 for validation; request_id; log.exception for unhandled; raise domain errors from services not HTTPException. MUST NOT: str(e) to clients; bare except; raise Exception('...'); return 200 with error flag for REST; catch CancelledError without re-raise; put FastAPI imports in deepest domain modules.
tests_required: Handler unit tests for AppError statuses; validation 422 shape; 500 does not include secret; domain function pytest.raises(NotFoundError); ASGI tests for auth error uniformity; ExceptionGroup logging if task groups used.
ci_gates: pytest; optional schema check that error responses match OpenAPI; grep ban for detail=str(e) and except Exception: pass in src.
skill_scan_signals: POSITIVE: exception_handler, AppError hierarchy, RequestValidationError handler, request_id in error body, raise X from e, safe client messages. NEGATIVE: except Exception as e: return str(e), raise Exception(, print traceback to response, HTTPException in repository layer, except: pass, missing 422 mapping.
skill_module_bullets:
- Typed AppError hierarchy; map at FastAPI handlers only.
- Validation → 422 with redacted details; never leak stacks.
- Stable error codes + request_id in JSON.
- Log once with exc_info at boundary.
- Reraise cancellation; chain causes with raise from.
- Result/Ok-Err optional for pure parsers — not default for all Python.
- Domain layer must not depend on FastAPI HTTPException.
action_items: 1) Error envelope schema in references/python.md. 2) Scan for str(e) client returns. 3) Standardize codes list. 4) Cross-link observability for log fields. 5) Document ExceptionGroup logging pattern.

conflicts_noted: Rust/functional communities push Result everywhere; idiomatic Python + FastAPI centers exceptions with edge mapping — follow Python idiom for services. HTTPException vs custom errors: both valid; custom better for reuse and non-HTTP callers (workers). ExceptionGroup handling APIs evolved (except* ) — prefer explicit logging helpers for readability in app code.
